findings.highlight: UhI don’t want either.
findings.evidenceJa: えいや、どっちもいらないけど
findings.governingReading: Shirou gives a flustered “No—neither,” before redirecting the conversation.
findings.explanation: The displayed English fuses “Uh” and “I,” damaging the opening response.

findings.highlight: You said something about there being another Master at our school.
findings.evidenceJa: そいつが何かしてるって
findings.governingReading: Shirou recalls that the other Master is doing something at school.
findings.explanation: The English omits the unknown Master’s action, reducing his question to mere existence.

findings.highlight: who’s doing things like what we just saw.
findings.evidenceJa: さっきみたいなコトを繰り返してるのよ
findings.governingReading: The Master has been repeatedly doing things like the attack they just witnessed.
findings.explanation: The English omits 繰り返してる, losing that the predation is recurrent.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka said she would’ve died if we hadn’t found her.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂が駆けつけなかったら命を落としていたという。
findings.governingReading: Rin said the girl would have died had Rin not rushed to her.
findings.explanation: The English changes Rin’s sole emergency intervention into Shirou and Rin jointly finding the victim.

findings.highlight: Wha[line3]using the students as sacrifices… Is that Master insane!?
findings.evidenceJa: な[line3]生徒を生け贄にするって、正気かそいつ！？
findings.governingReading: Shirou stammers in horror at sacrificing students.
findings.explanation: The English visibly fuses the broken “Wha” with “using.”

findings.highlight: No, you’re wrong.
findings.evidenceJa: いや、そうじゃないんだ。
findings.governingReading: Shirou says Rin’s anxious interpretation is not what he means.
findings.explanation: “You’re wrong” turns a correction of the misunderstanding into a direct accusation against Rin.

findings.highlight: This isn’t about that previous fight
findings.evidenceJa: 別にさっきのコトじゃなくてだな
findings.governingReading: Shirou insists his praise is not simply about what happened earlier.
findings.explanation: The English specifies a fight where さっきのコト leaves the recent matter implicit, prematurely fixing the referent.

findings.highlight: Please give me your best regards, Tohsaka.
findings.evidenceJa: これからよろしくな、遠坂
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks Rin to work well with him from here on.
findings.explanation: The stock literal “give me your best regards” is non-idiomatic and obscures the forward-looking partnership gesture.

findings.highlight: so at least be of some use to me, okay?
findings.evidenceJa: せいぜい役に立ってよね
findings.governingReading: Rin barbedly tells Shirou to make himself as useful as he possibly can.
findings.explanation: “At least” reverses せいぜい from a maximizer into a minimizer and weakens her demanding tease.

findings.highlight: We talk about unimportant stuff for a while.
findings.evidenceJa: とりとめのない会話が続く。
findings.governingReading: Their desultory, loosely connected conversation continues.
findings.explanation: The English judges the content unimportant instead of describing its rambling structure.

findings.highlight: As Tohsaka Rin is the head of the Tohsaka family, she is the supervisor of this land even though she’s young.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂の家を任されている遠坂凛は、この若さにしてここ一帯の管理人なのだそうだ。
findings.governingReading: Rin, entrusted with the Tohsaka house, is already manager of the surrounding territory at her young age.
findings.explanation: The English invents explicit family-head status and makes it the cause, replacing the source’s entrusted responsibility.

findings.highlight: I only know a bit of other things.
findings.evidenceJa: 他の魔術は名称とか概要とか、そんな事しか判らない。
findings.governingReading: Of other magecraft, Shirou knows only names and broad outlines.
findings.explanation: The English removes both concrete limits and even the explicit referent of other magecraft.

findings.highlight: is that something to be angry about?
findings.evidenceJa: 今のつっこむところか？
findings.governingReading: Shirou asks whether that was really the point for Rin to call out or retort to.
findings.explanation: The English replaces the comic conversational role of つっこむ with anger.

findings.highlight: magic is not something to hide desperately.
findings.evidenceJa: 相手がなんであれ、魔術は必死になって隠す事じゃない
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu taught that magecraft is not something to conceal desperately regardless of who the other person is.
findings.explanation: The English omits 相手がなんであれ, an important universal limit on Kiritsugu’s secrecy rule.

findings.highlight: If you’re taught by such a character, I can’t approve of you as a magus.
findings.evidenceJa: そんなヤツに鍛えられた貴方も、魔術師なんて認めないから
findings.governingReading: Rin refuses to recognize Shirou as a magus because he was trained by such a man.
findings.explanation: The English makes completed training conditional/present and weakens her volitional refusal to recognize him into inability to approve.

findings.highlight: It was my fault.
findings.evidenceJa: ちょっと、どうかしてた。
findings.governingReading: Rin apologizes that she was briefly not herself or acting strangely.
findings.explanation: The English replaces her account of altered behavior with a generic admission of blame.

findings.highlight: after a few years of study
findings.evidenceJa: 何年も魔術を鍛えていて
findings.governingReading: After training his magecraft for years and years.
findings.explanation: “A few years” narrows the emphatic 何年も and “study” weakens sustained practical training.

findings.highlight: your dad never did anything against that.
findings.evidenceJa: そのあたりの努力をまったくしなかった貴方の父親
findings.governingReading: Rin condemns Kiritsugu for making no effort at all toward succession safeguards.
findings.explanation: “Never did anything against that” suggests opposition rather than failure to undertake the required effort.

findings.highlight: ‘Magic’ of a magus isn’t just his magic.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師の『魔術』は、その魔術師だけのものじゃない。
findings.governingReading: A magus’s magecraft does not belong only to that individual magus.
findings.explanation: The repeated “magic” obscures the work’s 魔術 category and produces awkward English at a central inheritance explanation.

findings.highlight: a successor and an inheritor.
findings.evidenceJa: 後継者であり伝承者でもある
findings.governingReading: The child is both successor and transmitter or bearer of the tradition.
findings.explanation: “Inheritor” repeats receipt and loses 伝承者’s duty to carry and transmit the lineage onward.

findings.highlight: the duty of the ‘magus’
findings.evidenceJa: “魔術師”という家系の義務
findings.governingReading: The transformation of a human child is the duty of the lineage or house called “magus.”
findings.explanation: The English assigns the duty to an individual magus and omits the family-line institution Rin is defining.

findings.highlight: How much she sacrificed to train
findings.evidenceJa: どれだけ修練を積み重ね、どれだけ自分を犠牲にしてきたか
findings.governingReading: How much training Rin accumulated and how much of herself she separately sacrificed.
findings.explanation: The English collapses two parallel measures into sacrifice undertaken merely in order to train.

findings.highlight: That’s why I had to teach you a lesson!
findings.evidenceJa: つい灸を据えるっていうか、つっつきたくなったのっ！
findings.governingReading: Rin says she impulsively wanted to teach him a lesson—or rather, to poke and provoke him.
findings.explanation: The English adds necessity, removes つい, and deletes her self-correction into a more playful provoking impulse.

findings.highlight: Tohsaka ponders for a bit.
findings.evidenceJa: むー、とばつが悪そうに唸ったあと
findings.governingReading: Rin groans “mm” in visible embarrassment or awkwardness.
findings.explanation: The English replaces vocal embarrassment with silent thought.

findings.highlight: The man that almost got his head cut off by Saber that night.
findings.evidenceJa: あの夜、セイバーと打ち合い、その首を斬り落とされかけたサーヴァント。
findings.governingReading: The Servant who traded blows with Saber that night and nearly had his head cut off.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the near beheading but omits their direct exchange of blows.

findings.highlight: The man that tried to shoot Saber along with Berserker.
findings.evidenceJa: バーサーカーと戦うセイバーを無視して、もろともに葬り去ろうとした男。
findings.governingReading: The man who disregarded Saber fighting Berserker and tried to annihilate them both together.
findings.explanation: The English invents shooting as the mechanism and omits Archer’s disregard for Saber’s ongoing fight.

findings.highlight: I appreciate that.
findings.evidenceJa: 願ったり叶ったりだ。
findings.governingReading: Archer’s reciprocal dislike is exactly what Shirou could have wished for.
findings.explanation: “I appreciate that” loses the emphatic idiom of an outcome perfectly suiting his wishes.

findings.highlight: it’ll be great if you can help me.
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂が力を貸してくれるなら頼もしい
findings.governingReading: Shirou says Rin lending her power would be reassuring and dependable.
findings.explanation: Generic “great” removes his explicit reliance on Rin’s capability.

findings.highlight: It must be the same for Archer
findings.evidenceJa: それはアーチャーも同じなのか
findings.governingReading: Shirou wonders whether Archer feels the same aversion.
findings.explanation: “Must be” makes the reciprocal judgment categorical where のか leaves it as Shirou’s question or inference.

findings.highlight: he was also against the fact that I wanted to be a magus.
findings.evidenceJa: 魔術師になるのには反対してた
findings.governingReading: Kiritsugu opposed Shirou becoming a magus.
findings.explanation: The English makes the object of opposition the fact of Shirou’s desire, obscuring whether Kiritsugu opposed the wish or the resulting identity.

findings.highlight: Actually, he hid the fact that he was a magus.
findings.evidenceJa: というより、魔術師である事自体隠していたらしい。
findings.governingReading: Rather, it appears Kiritsugu concealed even the fact that he was a magus.
findings.explanation: The English changes らしい from reported inference to fact and というより from corrective refinement to “actually.”

findings.highlight: Then. She gets mad like it’s her own affair.
findings.evidenceJa: なぜか我がコトのように怒り出す。
findings.governingReading: For some reason, Rin begins getting angry as though it were her own affair.
findings.explanation: The English omits Shirou’s なぜか puzzlement and replaces it with a clumsy “Then.” fragment.

findings.highlight: it’s not my place to tell you something.
findings.evidenceJa: 衛宮くんをどうこう言える筈がなかった
findings.governingReading: Rin admits she had no standing to criticize or pass judgment on Shirou.
findings.explanation: “Tell you something” is vague and removes both criticism and the strength of her self-correction.
